author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Adam Greenman defeated longtime Pawtucket Mayor Don Grebien in Wednesday’s Democratic primary, according to unofficial Rhode Island Board of Elections results reported by NBC 10 News.

With all 28 reporting units submitting at least partial returns, Greenman had 3,633 votes, or about 54%, while Grebien had 3,055 votes, or about 46%. The totals remain unofficial until the canvass and certification process is complete.

Greenman, a former educator and nonprofit leader, campaigned on changes at City Hall and focused on education, affordability, public safety and quality-of-life issues. Grebien conceded and congratulated his challenger after serving as mayor since 2011. His current term will conclude after 16 years in the office.

No Republican candidate qualified for the mayoral ballot, according to the state candidate list cited by NBC 10. That could leave Greenman without a major-party opponent in the November 3 general election, though the certified ballot will determine the final field. Election officials will complete the official canvass before the result becomes final.
dek: Unofficial results showed Greenman ahead of Don Grebien 54% to 46%, setting up a likely transition after the incumbent’s 16 years in office.
headline: Adam Greenman defeats longtime Pawtucket mayor in Democratic primary
